name: manual_c5d812
claim: When mirroring a document set into a different co-located target directory, path prefixes get deliberately re-normalized for the new context (e.g. references/foo.md becomes foo.md once siblings are co-located in the mirror) -- never blindly copy lint or content fixes back to the canonical source without checking whether a given diff line is a deliberate context-specific normalization or a real defect.

decisions.notes: agent-envelope: agent=claude-main model=claude-sonnet-5 date=2026-09-17 | Caught before acting: orama-system PR#360's mirrored construction guide had references/2026-09-14-....md link paths stripped to 2026-09-14-....md (correct for co-located mirror files). A blind cp-based sync of my markdownlint line-wrap fixes back to the OpenClaw canonical copy would have silently re-broken those paths by reintroducing the mirror's stripped prefixes into the wrong context. Fixed line-wrapping independently in each location instead of diffing/copying wholesale.
